text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

Panel composition alone proves nothing. Planning departments skew female in many jurisdictions, and a four-person panel drawn from HR, elected officials and senior staff can easily be all women by chance. Raising it would make you look aggrieved and would undercut any legitimate complaint.

Also, your credential advantage may matter less than you think. Director roles are political and stakeholder-facing; a panel may genuinely rate "extensive public consultation experience" above a master's and a licence. That's a defensible judgement, not a pretext.

What *is* worth pursuing: the unanswered request. Follow up in writing, cite any access-to-information or policy right to selection records, and ask for feedback framed around future applications.
